reason: Part 2 of the authors' own two-part imaging-distortion series, evaluating technology-specific sources of measurement error in a new device-validation experiment, not re-testing a previously published finding from another study.
The GWAS hit was tested for replication with new genotyping/expression data in three independent cohorts (BIOS, KORA, GENOA), succeeding in one and failing in two.
New simulations reproduce prior DNS/literature results as a benchmark to validate a new numerical (overset grid) method, not to re-test a substantive scientific finding as the study's aim.

New resting-state fMRI data from 32 participants was collected to test whether previously identified arousal-linked dynamic connectivity states recur, finding centroids highly correlated with prior work.
The study validates a previously developed rs-fMRI disease-pattern biomarker (fPDRP) in a new sample/site, which is validation of a measurement method rather than re-testing a substantive finding.

New data from human iPSC-derived neurons were collected specifically to test whether a previously reported rodent finding (rPGRN-mediated neuroprotection) holds, an explicit re-test in a different population/system.
The study uses PK modelling to establish and confirm a dosing regimen as an internal positive-control reference across the authors' own studies, not to re-test an externally published finding.
This is a reliability/validity psychometric evaluation of a translated checklist, i.e., validating a measurement instrument, which is explicitly excluded.
A new coarse-grained force field is constructed and its reproduction of prior regime behavior is used to validate the modelling method itself, not to re-test a scientific finding.
Experiment 1 is explicitly described as 'a replication of previously reported rapid categorization effects,' using new behavioral data collected for that purpose.
A simulation environment is built and shown capable of reproducing previously reported experimental findings as a demonstration of the tool's validity, not as a standalone replication study.
The authors explicitly sought replication of their placental DNAm-adiposity association in an independent cohort using new methylation data.
